successors.name: Mongol Empire
successors.text: the Kyrgyz country of the Yenisei: Tuva, Khakassia and the Sayan foothills, turned into the Mongol "agricultural colony called Kem-Kemchik"

ledger.x: 763: the northern land leaves the Kyrgyz shape.
840: the Kyrgyz sack Ordu-Baliq and take the Orkhon.
850: the Kyrgyz leave the Mongolian plateau.
850: the Yenisei country to Lake Baikal.
1208: the Kyrgyz submit to the Mongols.

wars.name: Türk campaign against the Kyrgyz
wars.outcome: Second Turkic Khaganate page: Türk forces 'inflicted a crushing defeat on the Yenisei Kyrgyz'; the Kyrgyz ruler Bars Beg 'fell in battle' and his descendants 'were to remain vassals of the Göktürks for several generations'.

wars.name: Uyghur conquest of the Kyrgyz
wars.outcome: Bayanchur 'destroyed several of their trading outposts before defeating a Kyrgyz army and executing their khan' (Uyghur page); 'the Kyrgyz came under the rule of the Uyghur Khaganate' (Yenisei Kyrgyz page).

wars.name: Kyrgyz conquest of the Uyghur Khaganate
wars.outcome: Qasar seized the Uyghur throne in 839 with Shatuo help; his rival Kulug Bagha called in the Kyrgyz, who sacked Ordu-Baliq in 840 and beheaded Qasar.

certainty.note: Forest and mountain frontiers throughout; the pages date no treaty line.
